skill.name: gauntlet
skill.description: Guide evidence-driven reviews of code, APIs, infrastructure, designs, and agent workflows. Repair root causes only with authorization, then verify changes within a finite budget.
skill.summary: Review defects with evidence, track verification, and repair root causes within an authorized scope.

content.user_title: Review Defects and Verify Root-Cause Repairs
content.value_statement: Reviews can miss failure conditions or accept fixes without reliable evidence. Gauntlet guides scoped adversarial reviews, authorized repairs, and revision-bound verification within a finite budget.
actual_capabilities: Guide scoped reviews across correctness, security, reliability, accessibility, operations, and agent workflows.
Separate candidate defects from confirmed findings using reproductions, source traces, or other explicit evidence.
Guide authorized root-cause repairs with regression tests and neighboring-case checks.
Support independent sub-agent reviews or clearly labeled solo review passes.
Record tasks, findings, checks, revisions, and rounds in an optional standard-library SQLite tracker.
Invalidate recorded verification after target changes and compute scoped completion or budget-exhaustion outcomes.
limitations: The workflow cannot guarantee defect-free software or enforce host permissions.
The tracker records caller attestations; it does not run tests, authenticate approvals, or prove evidence.
The optional tracker requires Python 3.10 or later with sqlite3 and a private trusted directory.
Review quality across models and hosts is not benchmark-proven; unavailable tools limit executable verification.

use_cases.title: Review API Changes
use_cases.description: Examine API contracts, malformed inputs, failure paths, and affected consumers without modifying the implementation.

use_cases.title: Verify Reliability Repairs
use_cases.description: Trace retry or concurrency defects, authorize bounded repairs, and verify original failures plus neighboring schedules.

use_cases.title: Assess Agent Boundaries
use_cases.description: Review tool authority, untrusted content, evaluation integrity, and fallback behavior in an agent workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Small Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Gauntlet to review this change without modifying files. Check intended behavior and boundary cases. Separate confirmed defects from unresolved hypotheses.

prompt_templates.title: Review an API Contract
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this API change and its direct consumers with Gauntlet. Inspect malformed input, authorization, and error contracts. Record evidence and unavailable checks.

prompt_templates.title: Repair a Reproducible Defect
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Gauntlet to review and fix this reproducible defect within the stated scope. Preserve unrelated changes. Verify regressions and neighboring cases. Do not deploy.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Critical Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply Gauntlet at the critical tier to this tenant-isolation workflow. Remain read-only until repairs are authorized. Use independent reviewers when available. Bind evidence to snapshots.

output_examples.input: Review an API change without modifying files.
output_examples.output: Illustrative outcome: REVIEW_COMPLETE. The report separates substantiated defects from open hypotheses and lists scope, revision, evidence, executed checks, and untested surfaces.

output_examples.input: Review and repair a reproducible retry defect.
output_examples.output: Illustrative outcome: PASS_WITHIN_SCOPE after authorized repair, successful regression checks, and the required clean follow-up review. Remaining assumptions stay explicit.

output_examples.input: Verify a repair when its required database service is unavailable.
output_examples.output: Illustrative outcome: BLOCKED. Required execution evidence is unavailable. The report records the missing service and next action without claiming a verified repair.

best_practices: Define scope, intended behavior, exact revision, permissions, and review budget before starting.
Keep ledgers private, exclude them from version control, and redact secrets from evidence.
Revalidate checks after changes and use distinct follow-up attack strategies before reporting completion.
anti_patterns: Treating reviewer agreement or passing tests as proof that every defect is absent.
Weakening assertions, hiding failures, or recording proposed checks as executed.
Expanding scope, deploying changes, or extending review budgets without authorization.

faq.question: Does Gauntlet modify files during a review?
faq.answer: Reviews are read-only by default. Explicit review-and-fix authorization permits bounded local repairs, not deployments or unrelated changes.

faq.question: Are sub-agents required?
faq.answer: No. Gauntlet supports separate solo review passes and requires honest disclosure when independent verification is unavailable.

faq.question: Does the tracker require external services?
faq.answer: No. The optional tracker uses Python 3.10 or later and standard-library sqlite3. It needs no API key or network access.

faq.question: Does a tracker pass prove that tests ran?
faq.answer: No. The tracker validates recorded state and caller attestations. The host and reviewer must verify execution evidence and approvals.

faq.question: What happens when the target changes?
faq.answer: The helper invalidates checks and completed tasks, resets the clean streak, and reopens affected finding states for reassessment.

faq.question: Does Gauntlet guarantee secure or defect-free software?
faq.answer: No. Outcomes apply only to the declared scope and evidence. Review quality across hosts and models has not been benchmark-proven.
